name: Trade war & tariffs
summary: China's rare-earth control pause ends 10 Nov with no renewal announced
state: China's one-year suspension of its October 2025 rare-earth export controls, including the 0.1% content rule, expires on 10 Nov, and no renewal had been announced as of 6 Nov (Technology.org; Startup Fortune). Its April 2025 licensing rules for seven heavy rare earths remain in force. The wider US–China trade truce runs to 10 Jan 2027.
for_you: Manufacturers relying on rare-earth magnets face supply risk if the controls return; consumer effects would take months.
rubric_hit: Major new controls threatened between large economies = Watch

sources.title: Technology.org — China's rare-earth export pause: what ends on 10 November

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
